period.label: Report period
period.hint:
The period applies to closed tasks: only the ones closed on the chosen days are counted. It affects Completion in the statistics, the closed column of Team load, the lists of closed tasks and the weeks of Velocity (26 at most).

Open tasks, tasks in testing, overdue ones, Bugs, No estimate, hours, health, deadlines and Gantt show the current state and do not depend on the period.

The choice is remembered.

hints.stats:
Summary figures over the selected projects within your rights.
• Active Projects — projects with open tasks or tasks in testing.
• Completion — closed ÷ (open + half of the tasks in testing + closed).
• Open, In Test — tasks in the statuses of these groups (the groups are set in the status settings).
• Overdue — open and in-testing tasks whose due date is before today.
• Bugs — tasks in the statuses marked as Bugs.
• No Estimate — open tasks without an estimate.
Click a number to see its tasks.
hints.health:
A score of the projects from 0 to 100 over the active tasks — open and in testing.
Formula: 100 × (1 − (0.5 × overdue share + 0.3 × share in Bugs statuses + 0.2 × share without an estimate)).
Overdue tasks take off up to 50 points, Bugs up to 30, missing estimates up to 20.
80 and above is good, 50–79 needs attention, below 50 is bad.
Under the gauge you can see how many points each cause took off.
hints.velocity:
How many tasks were closed in each of the last 12 weeks, the current one included. A week runs from Monday to Sunday.
Tasks of the selected projects in a closed status are counted, by their closing date in Redmine. A reopened task does not count.
The tooltip of a bar shows the total estimate of the tasks closed that week.
When a period is chosen in the header of the tab, its weeks are shown — the last 26 at most.
hints.team_load:
The number of tasks of each member of the selected team over the selected projects.
• Open, In Test, closed — by status group.
• Overdue — open and in-testing tasks whose due date is before today.
• Bugs — tasks in the statuses marked as Bugs.
• High — tasks with the highest priority.
• No Estimate — open tasks without an estimate.
Click a number to see its tasks. The columns are set up with the button in the header.
hints.hours:
Hours over the tasks that are not closed, for each member of the selected team: the sum of estimates and the sum of time actually logged.
When the logged time is well above the estimate, the tasks are underestimated or dragging on. Employees without hours are not shown.
hints.bug_hours:
Time an employee logged on fixing bugs, over their tasks that are not closed.
The tooltip shows its share of all the time they logged: bug hours ÷ spent × 100.
Employees without bug hours are not shown.
hints.distribution:
A chart per project: how many open tasks each employee has.
A parent project and its nested ones are drawn as one chart — click it to see the breakdown by project. The grouping and the set of projects are changed with the button in the header; the choice is remembered.
hints.deadlines:
Tasks that are not closed and have a due date, sorted by urgency:
• Overdue — the due date is before today.
• Today — due today.
• 3 Days — due within the next three days.
• Week — due in 4–7 days.
A red stripe on the left marks a task with the highest priority. Click a tile to open the task card, the number to open the task in Redmine.
hints.gantt:
Tasks that are not closed and have a due date on a time scale, by deadline, 25 per page.
The main line is the planned period: from the start date (or the creation date when there is none) to the deadline; it says how many days were planned.
The extension in another colour is the delay from the deadline to today; it says by how many days the task is overdue.
The vertical line is today. The scale starts at most 90 days before today: the earlier part of a line is cut.
Click a name to open the task card.

hints.statuses:
Every Redmine status belongs to one of the groups. For example, New and In Progress are Open, Testing is In testing, Closed and Rejected are Closed.

The group decides which filter of the Tasks tab a task falls into and how it is counted in Analytics and in the sprint progress. Closed tasks are never overdue, tasks in testing do not get into the sprint backlog.

The setting is shared by all users and applies at once.
hints.sync:
Data comes from Redmine in two ways. Once per interval only the changes are fetched — it takes seconds. Once a day every project is read in full: this picks up tasks deleted in Redmine and hours logged for past dates.

The time of the full pass and a manual start are on the Workers tab of Administration. Only projects chosen by at least one user are synced.
hints.team:
The chosen members are your team. Team load is built over them, the list of assignees in a task is made of them, and they see your shared sprints.

The choice only narrows what the administrator allowed: a member beyond your rights cannot be added.
hints.alert_rules:
Every rule has two ways of delivery: the bell in the header and email. Emails do not go one by one: everything collected is sent as one message once per interval set by the administrator.

Your own edits in the dashboard do not notify you. Project rules work only in the projects chosen in the data settings. Events older than a week are not raised.
hints.thresholds:
A threshold is the number of tasks above which an indicator is alarming: its card on Analytics turns red and a warning appears above the widgets.

Without the per-project checkbox the threshold is compared with the total over all your projects. With it — with the number of tasks of each project.
hints.source_token:
Where to get the key: in Redmine open My account, find API access key on the right and press Show.

The key is stored encrypted. With it your task edits and comments go to Redmine under your own name instead of the service account.
hints.retention:
Once a day after a sync the system saves a snapshot: totals per member and the state of the tasks. The trend charts are built from the snapshots.

A cleanup deletes only the snapshots older than the retention period. Tasks, time entries, invoices and settings are not touched. Delete all snapshots removes the whole history — the charts start anew.
hints.mail:
Get the settings from your mail administrator. SSL/TLS encrypts the connection from the start, usually port 465. STARTTLS turns encryption on after connecting, usually port 587. No encryption is acceptable only inside your own network.

The dashboard address is needed for links: with it the number and the name of a task in an email open its card.
hints.users:
Rights add up in this order. An administrator can do everything. Others get rights from a role template; an individual setup (the shield icon) replaces the template. Then groups narrow the result: only the projects and members allowed by at least one group of the user remain.

Users link themselves to a Redmine member with a personal API key. The time zone is the default one until the user chooses their own.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.hint: The history of what users did in the system. Available to the administrator only.

debug_logs.title: Debug logs
debug_logs.hint: Requests of the users with debug logging turned on (the bug icon in the users table). Records are kept for 7 days. Press a row to see the request and response bodies.
debug_logs.help:
The mode is turned on for one user for 24 hours and turns off by itself. While it is on, every request of the user is recorded: the address, the request body, the server response, the code and the duration.

Passwords, keys and tokens in the records are replaced with asterisks. Files, bodies over 64 KB and anything that is not JSON are not saved — a note with the size is kept instead.

Recording runs in the background and does not slow the user down.
debug_logs.empty: No records. Turn debug logging on for a user in the users table.
debug_logs.clear_text: All of their records will be deleted. This cannot be undone.

connections.title: Connections
connections.hint: Connection settings of the database and the source system. Available to the administrator only. Only tested settings can be saved.

db.title: Database (PostgreSQL)
db.hint: The password is not shown back: leave the field as it is if it has not changed. Changing the database restarts the system.
db.confirm_title: Changing the database settings requires a restart of the system. Continue?
db.confirm_text: The restart takes up to a minute; the dashboard is unavailable to all users meanwhile. If the new database does not answer at start, the system returns to the previous one.
db.unchanged: The settings have not changed, no restart is needed

restart.hint: This may take up to a minute. Please do not close or reload the page.
restart.done: The system has restarted and runs with the saved settings
restart.rolled_back: The new database did not answer at start — the system returned to the previous settings. Check the database and try again.
restart.timeout: The server has not answered in two minutes. Check the containers on the server.

source.title: Source system (Redmine)
source.hint: The key and the password are not shown back: leave the fields as they are if they have not changed. Changes apply at once, without a restart.
source.saved: Saved. A sync with the new settings has started.

errors.DB_FIELDS_REQUIRED: Fill in the host, the port and the user. The port is a number from 1 to 65535.
errors.INVALID_DB_NAME: Database name: latin letters, digits, underscore and hyphen.
errors.DB_CONNECTION_FAILED: Could not connect to the database.
errors.DB_NO_ADMIN: This database holds no dashboard data or no administrator — nobody could log in after the restart. Give the database the system has already worked with.
errors.CONFIG_SAVE_FAILED: Could not save the settings on the server.
